subject.title: feat(gateway): deliver plugin approvals to paired iOS devices via APNs

question: Should plugin approval title and description be permitted in user-visible APNs payloads, or must native notifications remain generic until an authenticated client fetches the approval details?
rationale: The plugin API does not enforce that caller-authored approval text is safe for APNs relays, Apple infrastructure, lock screens, or mirrored watches, so the permanent confidentiality contract requires explicit owner intent.

options.title: Keep APNs copy generic
options.body: Send only generic approval-required text and fetch title and description after the authenticated client opens the approval, matching the safer exec-notification pattern.

options.title: Allow descriptive alerts
options.body: Accept plugin-authored title and description in APNs after documenting the expanded visibility contract and proving callers cannot place sensitive metadata there.

options.title: Pause for client design
options.body: Hold the server change until the companion iOS implementation defines capability negotiation, authenticated detail loading, and notification privacy behavior.

recommendation.title: Keep APNs copy generic
recommendation.body: Send only generic approval-required text and fetch title and description after the authenticated client opens the approval, matching the safer exec-notification pattern.

likelyOwner.reason: The history and proposal connect this person most directly to the paired-device APNs and plugin-approval design surfaces involved in the decision.
